thread:
emma_support: heads-up — acme-corp just flagged that their daily totals in the Billing -> Usage chart are consistently shifted by 7 hours vs the CSV they export. chart shows 03/02 but CSV rows are dated 03/01. org TZ = America/Los_Angeles. screenshot: https://redwood.screenshot/abc123 :eyes:
rajesh_sre: thanks. can you paste one example CSV row and the chart hover timestamp so we can compare raw values? also, do they use our hosted export or api-based export?
devon_analytics: they used the Console CSV export (UI) and also hit the /v1/usage/export endpoint. attached small sample they sent:```2026-03-01T02:15:00-08:00,account=acme-corp,tokens=4321
2026-03-01T18:05:00-08:00,account=acme-corp,tokens=987```
rajesh_sre: ok looking at that — UI CSV preserves local offset (-08:00) in rows, but our dashboard aggregation appears to be bucketing by day_start=00:00Z (UTC), not org-local midnight. that explains 7 hour shift.
maria_product: is this a regression? we rolled the analytics refactor two weeks ago. need P0 if it affects billing charts.
metrics-bot: ingestion-lag alert for org acme-corp between 2026-03-01T00:00Z and 2026-03-02T00:00Z — avg lag 5m, no drops. (alert id: MTR-20260302-77)
devon_analytics: repro steps I ran locally: 1) create two events at 2026-03-01T06:00Z and 2026-03-01T20:00Z with account=acme-corp; 2) hit /v1/usage/summary?date=2026-03-01&tz=America/Los_Angeles -> expected both events on 03-01, UI shows one on 03-01 and one on 03-02 because aggregation used date_trunc('day', timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC').
rajesh_sre: thanks, that pinpoints it. the refactor switched some materialized view queries to use server_ts (UTC) without applying org_tz mapping. I can put up a one-line fix to apply timezone conversion before grouping.
maria_product: please create a bug ticket and mark rollback criteria. also need communication for affected customers (likely those with non-UTC org tz).
rajesh_sre: creating ticket RNFD-5123 now, assigning to me. workaround for support: instruct customers to use the export endpoint with explicit start/end in UTC, e.g. `/v1/usage/export?start=2026-03-01T00:00:00-08:00&end=2026-03-02T00:00:00-08:00` — that will preserve their intended day window until we patch.
emma_support: noted, I'll send acme-corp the workaround and ask for the export id they used. any ETA?
rajesh_sre: quick patch target today (hotfix) then a follow-up change to tests. if patch is blocked we'll roll back the refactor in analytics service.
deploy-bot: deploy confirmed: analytics-service v2.14.0 -> v2.14.1 (2026-03-01T14:07:12Z) by @devon_analytics (deploy id dpl-20260301-137)
metrics-bot: query-run: `SELECT date_trunc('day', (timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')) as day_utc, count(*) FROM events WHERE org = 'acme-corp' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-03-03' GROUP BY 1;` returned days labelled in UTC rather than org_tz.
maria_product: please add affected org list to the ticket (quick scan: ~12 customers with America/* or Asia/* org tz configured during March window). also prepare a short customer note draft for support.
rajesh_sre: added list and draft. I'll attach a follow-up script to recompute aggregates with correct tz for the backfill.
emma_support: sent workaround to customer and opened support case referencing RNFD-5123. customer provided export id E-3321 and sample CSV. will post if they confirm fix. :thumbsup:
rajesh_sre: will update this thread when patch is live. TL;DR cause = aggregation used UTC day boundaries instead of org-local midnight; fix = apply org time zone when truncating to day before summarizing.
